caption: The video captures a fixed macro view of a crystalline deposit already present on a surface. A dark olive-brown upper field is scattered with soft, out-of-focus bright highlights, while a pale grey-white layer fills the lower area. Between them lies a horizontal band of fine, needle-like and dendritic white crystals standing upright. Throughout the excerpt the crystal band itself keeps its shape, neither extending nor branching. The change is confined to the lower zone, where a faint pale haze and scattered fine specks gradually thicken, softening the dark shadowed strip beneath the needles. The surface texture thus builds slowly and continuously, with no abrupt onset, contact, or completion visible within the clip.
relations: Faint pale haze and fine specks accumulating in the lower zone gradually soften the dark shadowed strip beneath the needles.
The upright needle-like crystal band maintains its shape, neither extending nor branching during the accumulation.
Continuous slow surface texture buildup in the lower layer occurs without abrupt onset, contact, or completion.
